summary: Round 4 testing — three polish items: (1) ExplainFinding testid prefix alignment (-btn vs -out), (2) in-memory LRU cache for AI explanations keyed by finding+context hash, (3) SSE heartbeat ping every 8 tokens during live streaming. Backend: 38/38 pytest tests pass (13+9+10+6). 6 new Round-4 tests all green: first call uncached & slow (>1s), second call cached & fast (<2s) with byte-for-byte identical text, cache key isolation on different engine_metadata, /api/inspector/explain-cache/stats returns {entries,max:64}, DELETE clears (and reports cleared count), and >=1 'event: ping' frame appears in live stream. Frontend: all 5 finding cards in InspectorReport now expose buttons with testids ending in '-btn' (e.g. explain-FUEL_SUB_MS_PW-0-btn) and output containers ending in '-out' (explain-FUEL_SUB_MS_PW-0-out). Zero testids violate the pattern. Selectors [data-testid$='-btn'] and [data-testid$='-out'] cleanly separate buttons from outputs. UI cache UX verified: first explain took 10.6s, after × close + re-click the cached replay completed in 1.6s (~6.6x speedup) with the same content rendered.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py is now 765 lines — getting close to the 700-line guideline. Cache helpers (_explain_cache_key, _explain_cache_put, OrderedDict + GET/DELETE endpoints) and the explainer endpoint could be split into a dedicated /app/backend/explainer.py module for cleanliness. Non-blocking.
Cache key uses sha1 of json.dumps(... default=str). Acceptable for short-lived process cache; not collision-sensitive at 64 entries.

Heartbeat 'event: ping' frames are correctly emitted every 8 tokens; the frontend ExplainFinding.jsx safely ignores any event != token/error/done so ping frames are silently dropped (verified visually — no UI artefacts).
Cache is process-local and lost on backend restart — acknowledged in code comment and acceptable per spec.

Minor: import block for OrderedDict/hashlib/json placed AFTER the explain_finding route handler. Functionally OK because the handler resolves names at call-time and the imports execute at module load (before any request), but stylistically these belong at the top of the file.

success_rate.frontend: 100% — testid alignment + cache UX both verified visibly

seed_data_creation: Round-4 pytest creates and reuses one finding-payload context (cache fills to 2 entries before clear). UI run created TEST_R4_UI profile + 1 inspector report (left in DB, harmless).
